description: The 'commits' dataset provides a detailed record of changes made to software projects, capturing essential metadata and the extent of modifications. Each entry in the dataset represents a unique commit, identified by a 'commit_id', and is associated with a specific 'project_key'. This dataset is particularly useful for software development teams, project managers, and researchers interested in analyzing software development practices, tracking project progress, or studying the impact of individual contributions. Key features include the 'author' of the commit, the 'timestamp' indicating when the commit was made, and quantitative data on the number of 'added_files', 'added_lines', 'removed_files', 'removed_lines', and 'changed_files'. These metrics provide insights into the scale and nature of changes, helping to assess the complexity and impact of each commit. The dataset can be used for various purposes, such as generating project reports, conducting code quality analysis, or supporting machine learning models that predict software development trends. Its structured format allows for easy integration with data analysis tools and software development platforms.
shortDesc: Software project commit dataset with metadata and changes.

columns.name: project_key
columns.comment: Unique identifier for the software project.

columns.name: author
columns.comment: Name or identifier of the commit author.

columns.name: timestamp
columns.comment: Time when the commit was made, in milliseconds.

columns.name: added_files
columns.comment: Number of files added in the commit.

columns.name: added_lines
columns.comment: Number of lines added in the commit.

columns.name: removed_files
columns.comment: Number of files removed in the commit.

columns.name: removed_lines
columns.comment: Number of lines removed in the commit.

columns.name: changed_files
columns.comment: Number of files changed in the commit.
